question: What bodies become possible with this capability, and what remains outside it?

ca.title: A neighbourhood makes the next row
ca.inherit: Arrays, binary state, clocks and repeatable beginnings.
ca.addition: One local rule reads an ordered neighbourhood; answers go into a separate next-state buffer.
ca.encounter: Begin with ca_rule_explorer. The rug and line network remain as further encounters with other mechanisms.
ca.experiment: Predict one marked cell, STEP, then change the seed while keeping the rule. Inspect the wrapped edge.
ca.crack: Which distinctions survive the neighbourhood? A count loses information that ordered left/self/right bits can preserve.
ca.transfer: Explain a new three-bit case and show why writing into the old row could change later answers.
ca.next_action: Complete the prepared Introduction engine review. Treat the rug and network as returns after the row, so the first explanation does not have to teach three mechanisms at once.
ca.readiness: Source prepared; Introduction engine review pending.

ca.title: Give the past a direction
ca.inherit: The one-dimensional row and its local rule.
ca.addition: Retain generations and map their order onto depth. Drawing history is distinct from adding spatial neighbours.
ca.encounter: ca_bridge with study:history: a desk, support tiles and ornamental lattice share one record. The four other works remain in the rear gallery.
ca.experiment: Read the same Rule 30 generation on a flat record and on the bridge. Predict the next row before following the structure.
ca.crack: A visible neighbour may be an earlier moment. A drawn cube also needs collision before it can carry a body.
ca.transfer: Identify which axis is time and which values belong to the same current state.
ca.next_action: The shared history and the following Life-dish application are implemented. Review these in a headset later; continue through the completed exchange study to CA_EdgeOfChaos.
ca.readiness: Implemented: one 15-site, 24-row Rule 30 history, six controls, three mappings and full-size retained lab; real desktop checks and museum captures at ca-history-bridge.html.

ca.title: A pattern travels; its cells stay
ca.inherit: A row, an update schedule and the distinction between state and its displayed history.
ca.addition: A two-dimensional present with eight neighbours; collective patterns persist or travel through fixed addresses.
ca.encounter: game_of_life_petri with study:addresses: one present in a dish and floor, three fixed cell addresses driving three lamps. All five other works remain.
ca.experiment: STEP a clean glider; follow A and the travelling figure separately. Compare BLINKER and MEET. Disconnect LINK while continuing the automaton.
ca.crack: What is the travelling body if none of its cell addresses travels with it? The state remains binary despite the room ID.
ca.transfer: Distinguish an oscillator, a travelling pattern and a displaced drawing; predict a local B3/S23 update.
ca.next_action: Primary implemented and desktop reviewed. Headset and retained secondary encounters remain. CA_ExpandingSpace is now desktop reviewed; the live field is now reviewed; continue to CA_EdgeOfChaos.
ca.readiness: 30 Godot desktop checks passed; fixed-address lamps, clean comparisons and revised final. All six works retained. Photographs and remote model at ca-life-addresses.html.

ca.title: A cell takes time to disappear
ca.inherit: A stored state, a neighbourhood and a recognisable pattern.
ca.addition: A three-dimensional neighbourhood and a refractory state. These are two additions, so demonstrate them in two passes.
ca.encounter: The retained structure_growth study and its state/height finish comparison.
ca.experiment: First locate face, edge and corner neighbours around one address. Then follow 1 → 2 → 0 and compare a fading cell with an empty cell under the same active-neighbour count.
ca.crack: Presence, participation and visibility differ. Changing the finish can conceal distinctions without changing the state.
ca.transfer: Explain why an empty cell with seven active neighbours can be born while a fading cell must first become empty.
ca.next_action: Keep the completed study. Add a neighbourhood witness or slice if depth cannot be read; optimise its measured 144 ms full-volume update before headset acceptance.
ca.readiness: 21 desktop checks and real screenshots; full-volume performance and headset review pending.

ca.title: The visitor enters the update
ca.inherit: Persistence, disappearance, fields, thresholds and the player body from earlier chapters.
ca.addition: A surface stores graded health; proximity affects it and a threshold changes collision. The observer becomes an input to the system.
ca.encounter: decaying_bridge, with the existing tree, crossway and chair retained as further architectural constructions.
ca.experiment: Approach from a safe rim, wait, withdraw. Compare health, appearance and actual support. Hold distance while varying observation time.
ca.crack: The bridge responds to a tracked body origin, not measured weight. SYNC and SCAN expose whether a newly recovered neighbour is available during this pass or the next.
ca.transfer: Tell whether a change came from proximity, elapsed time, neighbours or the collision threshold.
ca.next_action: Primary implemented: revisit in a headset later and review the retained gallery. The live field in CA_SoftRules is now desktop reviewed; continue to CA_EdgeOfChaos.
ca.readiness: 36 real Godot checks, including tracked-body falling and ramp recovery. Witness, matched schedule comparison and shared health frieze built; photographs and remote model at ca-proximity.html.

ca.title: What can one cell exchange?
ca.inherit: Graded health, synchronous arrays and display mappings.
ca.addition: Two concentrations and a five-point exchange term; local reaction, feed and removal continue when exchange is disabled.
ca.encounter: rd_artifact: a held matched Gray–Scott study with table fields and curved wall coatings. The clockmaker remains a second primary diagram; all six authored works now load.
ca.experiment: Follow W outside the seed: STEP with B exchange OFF, then toggle it ON and compare matching beginnings. Change VIEW and COAT without advancing the state.
ca.crack: Fractional values still occupy a finite periodic lattice; an 8-bit colour mapping can hide their differences. A static fractional ring is not a running Lenia field.
ca.transfer: Distinguish neighbourhood exchange, local reaction, an intervention and the projection of a field onto architecture.
ca.next_action: Primary study implemented and desktop reviewed. The matched intervention in CA_EdgeOfChaos is now desktop reviewed; headset and retained-secondary reviews remain.
ca.readiness: 37 Godot checks: first-step arithmetic, legacy-solver agreement, full-field equality, GPU texture mapping, eight real controls and physical walking. Photographs, remote model and two book passages at ca-soft-rules.html.

ca.title: Does a difference spread?
ca.inherit: Neighbour coupling, chance, replay and the distinction between an observation and a claim.
ca.addition: An experiment on sensitivity: compare matched runs, change one cell, measure the difference over a stated duration.
ca.encounter: self_organization_ca; retain the screen, disease, crack and fog works as differently specified systems.
ca.experiment: Compare paired runs with shared address-indexed forcing and one altered cell. Switch integer/fractional storage; compare affected count, maximum difference and magnification. Spatial Z does not advance time.
ca.crack: The new controls separate pull and disturbance. Integer storage can erase a trace; fractional storage can spread it while its maximum fades. Read display gain and count tolerance before naming a regime.
ca.transfer: Distinguish a stationary pattern, an observation-budget stop, a repeating cycle and a growing difference; state which measure supports the claim.
ca.next_action: Primary implemented and desktop reviewed. Revisit in a headset and develop the four retained secondary works. Next active hall: Fractal_Recursion.
ca.readiness: Implemented: 45 Godot checks, paired 11-cube volumes, twelve controls, spatial slices and a shared difference floor. All five works retained; review at ca-edge-difference.html.

ca.title: The same resemblance, another construction
ca.inherit: Repeated local updates, visible history and controlled comparison.
ca.addition: Compare local evolution with explicit recursive copying; establish the hinge into the fractals chapter.
ca.encounter: The existing ca_rule_explorer and sierpinski_pyramid. Keep the historical ID while giving the encounter an accurate public title.
ca.experiment: Name one relation among gaps in Rule 90 history, then test that relation in the recursive pyramid. Change the row seed and see which resemblance survives.
ca.crack: Related silhouettes need not share a procedure. The pyramid and the flat history need not match in every relation; neither proves a circuit or computational universality.
ca.transfer: Explain one construction using neighbour updates and the other using smaller copies and a stopping condition.
ca.next_action: Review and restore this omitted map at the CA exit when its spatial and textual links are ready. It currently exists in the curriculum but not in the seven-hall active museum route.
ca.readiness: Two existing placements; absent from active route. Restoration proposed, not applied.

randomness.title: A draw has a beginning
randomness.experiment: Repeat the same beginning; discard one draw and inspect which neighbours change.

randomness.title: A measure keeps only some differences
randomness.experiment: Sort the same multiset: identify what the entropy reading retains and what spatial relations it loses.

randomness.title: Chance acts inside a permitted set
randomness.experiment: Name a cube outside the selectable set; inspect how the set changes after removal.

randomness.title: A choice accumulates into a path
randomness.experiment: Distinguish the state used by the next step from the longer trail shown to the visitor.

randomness.title: Sampling makes a distribution visible
randomness.experiment: Keep the samples and change the bins before attributing a changed picture to a changed generator.

randomness.title: A distribution becomes a body
randomness.experiment: Ask which stem/cap combinations the recipe cannot produce; vary one mapping, not only the seed.

randomness.title: Chance changes what an action affords
randomness.experiment: Predict a crossing from known timing, then identify which sampled wait changed the outcome.

noise.title: Which changes remain possible?
noise.addition: Address, domain and relation among samples
noise.experiment: Follow point constraints into independent versus related samples. Give nearby addresses comparable spacing.

noise.title: Where does change enter the body?
noise.experiment: Compare the columns without assuming every moving surface uses the same process.

noise.title: A value can become different attributes
noise.addition: Sample versus mapping to colour or form
noise.experiment: Give the same values two outputs; locate what changed in the mapping.

noise.title: A value becomes occupied space
noise.experiment: Keep field and seed fixed; change the threshold and inspect a named empty as well as occupied address.

noise.title: A composed field dresses a room
noise.addition: Layering and a shared spatial application
noise.experiment: Trace which part of the sum reaches walls and objects; keep floor support separate from its appearance.

noise.title: Where is the field being read?
noise.experiment: Stand inside the sphere and compare an attached address with an address shared with the surrounding space.

noise.title: The field carries a body
noise.experiment: Keep player and route fixed; compare effort, access and concealment across different terrain settings.

noise.title: What makes a comparison fair?
noise.addition: Matched samples and the limits of the organic filter
noise.experiment: Match coordinates and mapping before naming a difference; ask which desired behaviour requires more than a sampled field.
